project.title: Sequential Rademacher Complexity
project.description:
We consider the problem of sequential prediction and provide tools to study the minimax
value of the associated game. Classical statistical learning theory provides several useful
complexity measures to study learning with i.i.d. data. Our proposed sequential complex-
ities can be seen as extensions of these measures to the sequential setting. The developed
theory is shown to yield precise learning guarantees for the problem of sequential predic-
tion. In particular, we show necessary and suﬃcient conditions for online learnability in
the setting of supervised learning. Several examples show the utility of our framework: we
can establish learnability without having to exhibit an explicit online learning algorithm

nodes.title: Minimax Theorem
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$ be Banach spaces. Let $A\subset \mathcal{A}$ be nonempty, weakly compact, and convex, and let $B\subset \mathcal{B}$ be nonempty and convex. Let $g:\mathcal{A}\times\mathcal{B}\to \reals$ be concave with respect to $b\in B$ and convex and lower-semicontinuous with respect to $a\in A$, and weakly continuous in $a$ when restricted to $A$. Then
$$

		\sup_{b\in B} \inf_{a\in A} g(a,b) = \inf_{a\in A} \sup_{b\in B} g(a,b).
$$

nodes.title: Value of Online Learning
nodes.statement:
The minimax value of the online learning game with loss function $\ell$ is defined as
$$
	\mathrm{Val}_T(\mathcal{F}, \ \mathcal{Z})  ~:=~ \inf_{q_1\in \mathbf{Q}}\sup_{z_1\in\ \mathcal{Z}} \mathbb{E}_{f_1 \sim q_1} \cdots  \inf_{q_T\in \mathbf{Q}}\sup_{z_T\in \mathcal{Z}} \mathbb{E}_{f_T \sim q_T} \left[ \sum_{t=1}^T \ell(f_t,z_t) - \inf_{f\in \mathcal{F}}\sum_{t=1}^T \ell(f,z_t)\right] \ .
$$

nodes.title: Value to Sequential Rademacher
nodes.statement:
The minimax value of an online learning game with loss $\ell$ is bounded as
$$
\frac{1}{T}\mathrm{Val}_T(\mathcal{F}) \le 2\, \mathrm{Rad}_T(\ell(\mathcal{F}))
$$
where $\ell(\mathcal{F}) = \{\ell(f,\cdot): f\in\mathcal{F}\}$.

nodes.title: Sequential Covering Number
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathbf{z}$ be a $\mathcal{Z}$-valued tree of depth $n$ and let $\mathcal{F} \subset \mathbb{R}^{\mathcal{Z}}$.  A covering at scale $\delta$ is a set of binary real-valued trees $\mathbf{v}^1, \cdots, \mathbf{v}^N$ such that for all $f \in \mathcal{F}$ and all $\epsilon \in \{ \pm 1 \}^n$, there is some $j$ such that
$$
      \left\|f(\mathbf{z}(\epsilon)) - \mathbf{v}^j(\epsilon) \right\|^2\leq n\delta^2.
$$
  The covering number $N(\mathcal{F}, \delta, \mathbf{z})$ of a class $\mathcal{F}$ for a tree $\mathbf{z}$ at scale $\delta$ is the minimal $N$ such that there exists a $\delta$-covering of size $N$.

nodes.title: Sequential Rademacher Complexity
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathcal{F} \subset \mathbb{R}^{\mathcal{Z}}$. The sequential Rademacher complexity of the function class $\mathcal{F}$ is defined as 
$$
 \mathrm{Rad}_T(\mathcal{F}) = \frac{1}{T} \sup_{\mathbf{z}} \mathbb{E}_\epsilon\left[\sup_{f \in \mathcal{F}} \sum_{t=1}^T \epsilon_t f(\mathbf{z}_t(\epsilon)) \right]
$$
Where $\mathbf{z} = (\mathbf{z}_1,\ldots,\mathbf{z}_T)$ is a $\mathcal{Z}$-valued tree of depth $T$ and $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_T$ are drawn as Rademacher random variables.
